nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure 1, the 1.25 V vs. RHE (anodic, A₁) were identified as the pre-oxidation of Co²⁺ to Co³⁺, while the potentials at 1.47 (anodic, A₂) and 1.40 V (cathodic, C) belong to the redox couple of Co³⁺/Co⁴⁺.

nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure S1, to be specific, the anodic peak in the first cycle appears at 1.25 V for V_O-Co₃O₄... The absence of the cathodic peak of the reduction of Co³⁺ to Co²⁺ suggests that the surface of V_O-Co₃O₄ underwent an irreversible surface reconstruction... the larger K_s (redox constant) of V_O-Co₃O₄ (0.32 s⁻¹) compared with that of pure Co₃O₄ (0.29 s⁻¹)

nodes.source_text: the specific activity (current per Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET, Figure S5) area or electrochemical active surface area (ECSA, Figure S6) of the electrocatalysts for OER was achieved. We normalized the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) polarization curves with BET and ECSA, as shown in Figures S7 and S8, indicating the preferable catalytic performance on V_O - Co_3O_4 and confirming that the intrinsic activity was improved due to the surface enriched oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV shows pre-oxidation of Co²⁺ to Co³⁺ at 1.25 V vs RHE for V_O-Co₃O₄, lower than pure Co₃O₄, with Ks = 0.32 s⁻¹ indicating higher OH* binding strength.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1B, the larger K_s (redox constant) of V_O-Co₃O₄ (0.32 s⁻¹) compared with that of pure Co₃O₄ (0.29 s⁻¹) indicates the higher binding strength of V_O to the OH* intermediate.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando EIS shows lower R_total for V_O-Co₃O₄ beyond 1.15 V vs RHE, indicating faster OH* adsorption kinetics; phase peak shifts confirm faster Co-OOH* deprotonation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The R_total of V_O - C_0₃O₄ is lower than that of pure Co₃O₄ beyond 1.15 V, demonstrating a much faster kinetics in adsorbed of OH ions during OER (Figure 2C).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ EPR shows stronger Co(IV) signal (g=2.23) at 1.45 V for V_O-Co₃O₄ and more Co²⁺ consumption during pre-oxidation compared to pure Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with pure Co₃O₄, the stronger peak intensity of Co(IV) -containing species (g value at 2.23) for V_O - Co₃O₄ shows that there is more Co(IV) coupling OOH* intermediate formation at 1.45 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows nearly no macroscopic morphology change for both pure Co₃O₄ and V_O-Co₃O₄ under OER conditions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Note that there is nearly no macroscopic change for both pure Co₃O₄ and V_O - Co₃O₄ under the OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi-operando XRD confirms cubic spinel Co₃O₄ structure (JCPDS No. 43-1003) maintained for both catalysts through OER process.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns for both pure Co₃O₄ (Figure S16A) and V_O - Co₃O₄ (Figure S16B) can be indexed to cubic spinel Co₃O₄ (JCPDS No. 43-1003).

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows characteristic Co₃O₄ phonon modes at 197, 485, 524, 620, 691 cm⁻¹ maintained during OER with no impurity phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman bands at ca. 197, 485, 524, 620, and 691 cm⁻¹ can be indicated to the F¹₂g,E₂g,F²₂g,F₂g and A₁g phonon modes of typically structured Co₃O₄, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM/HRTEM shows both catalysts maintain crystal structure with little lattice mismatch after OER testing; V_O-Co₃O₄ self-reconstructs to crystalline CoOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM images showed that they mostly maintained the crystal structure with little lattice mismatch, disorder, or reconstruction.

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi-operando XPS shows initial Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio of 1.16 for V_O-Co₃O₄ (higher than pure Co₃O₄) decreasing to ~0.95 during OER; O 1s O2/O1 ratio decreases from 5.4 to 1.1 as oxygen vacancies fill with OH⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with pure Co₃O₄, the relative content of Co²⁺ for V_O - Co₃O₄ was increased and the rate of Co²⁺ / Co³⁺ was 1.16 prior to electrochemical tests. ... the initial ratio of O2/O1 for V_O - Co₃O₄ was about 5.4 and the ratio decreased quickly ... and subsequently maintained at 1.1 from 1.45 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Co K-edge XANES shows faster Co oxidation (edge shift) for V_O-Co₃O₄; EXAFS shows ΔN/N of Co-O increases significantly at 1.15 V (onset 1.45 V) vs pure Co₃O₄ (1.55 V), confirming faster reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the relative changes of coordination number (ΔN/N) of Co-O for V_O - Co₃O₄ significantly immediately increased after immersion in the electrolyte at 1.15 V and then increased further ... The largest ΔN/N was found at the onset of OER at 1.45 V.
